source.title: Split-Boost Neural Networks
source.authors: R. G. Cestari; Gabriele Maroni; Loris Cannelli; Dario Piga; Simone Formentin

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Figure values are not recoverable from the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: Compares test performance under a different training strategy and reports a generalization result on natural data; it does not test any listed version's specific conditions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-cost comparisons for split-boost and a regularized feed-forward network. It does not test random-label memorization, width, architecture comparisons, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example removal.
record.test_reason: The study compares split-boost with regularized feed-forward training on insurance-charge regression. It cites original sources as background but tests none of V1–V8. Lower test cost for its proposed method does not establish any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors: in this case study, split-boost improves predictive performance, reaches convergence in fewer epochs and less total training time despite slower epochs, and is claimed to counteract overfitting implicitly.
record.recipe_differences: Split-boost divides the training set into two parts, solves separate least-squares problems for output-layer weights, and updates hidden-layer weights by gradient descent; the comparison network uses explicit regularization.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports sensitivity analysis for learning rate and, for the feed-forward network, the regularization parameter; both networks use γ = 0.1 and the feed-forward comparison uses λ = 0.01.

fits_no_version.finding: On insurance-charge regression, split-boost achieved lower test cost than the tuned regularized feed-forward comparator in 72% of 50 randomized data splits.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Split-boost can improve held-out regression performance over regularized feed-forward training for the tested two-layer, ten-hidden-unit network and dataset.

record.problems: The evidence is limited to one real-world regression dataset and one two-layer network configuration. The 50-randomization comparison is described as statistically lower, but no test, p-value, confidence interval, or numerical test-cost values are given in the text; the boxplot is figure-only.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately quantified test-performance results are stated in the text. Figures 5–8 contain plotted values that are not specified numerically in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance under random versus natural labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects on held-out error, including training-set size and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness as a predictor of generalization gaps and its comparison with other measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The implicit-regularization interpretation is the authors' conclusion; the experiment does not isolate its mechanism. Splitting training data into two subsets is not a batch-size intervention testing V5.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fit or held-out performance comparison for random and natural labels.
No network-width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.

rows.subject: Split-boost neural network
rows.stage_stated: trained on the medical insurance dataset; re-trained using the union of the previous training and validation sets
rows.operation_detail: Compared test cost after the retraining procedure against the regularized feed-forward network across 50 randomizations of training, validation, and test sets.
rows.baseline: Best regularized feed-forward neural network with λ = 0.01
rows.value: Split-boost test cost is lower in 72% of the cases; statistically lower
rows.note: The text gives the direction and frequency of the comparison but no test-cost values or statistical test details.
rows.check: This is the study's own method-performance comparison, not evidence for a listed version. The reported 72% win rate is correctly extracted, but the row should be excluded from claim-evidence rows. Statistical superiority is asserted without a named test, p-value, or confidence interval.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
